questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the origin of the universe:
1. Edwin Hubble's observations of receding galaxies in the 1920s supported the idea of an expanding universe.
2. The cosmic microwave background radiation was discovered by Penzias and Wilson.
3. The Big Bang is estimated to have occurred about 4.6 billion years ago.
questions.e: Galaxies moving apart point back to a hot dense beginning, and the leftover glow was detected as the cosmic microwave background in 1965. The Big Bang is dated at roughly 13.8 billion years; 4.6 billion years is the age of the Earth.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 2

questions.q:
Arrange the following theories on the origin of the Earth and solar system in the chronological order of their proposal:
1. Planetesimal hypothesis of Chamberlin and Moulton
2. Nebular hypothesis of Laplace
3. Interstellar dust hypothesis of Otto Schmidt
4. Tidal hypothesis of Jeans and Jeffreys
questions.e: Laplace revised the nebular idea in the late 1700s; Chamberlin and Moulton followed in the early 1900s; Jeans and Jeffreys proposed the tidal model in the 1910s-20s, and Schmidt's interstellar dust idea came in the 1940s.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 2; Savindra Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about seismic waves:
1. P-waves can travel through solids, liquids and gases.
2. S-waves travel faster than P-waves.
3. S-waves are not recorded beyond about 105 degrees from the epicentre because they cannot pass through the liquid outer core.
questions.e: P-waves are compressional and pass through all states of matter, whereas S-waves are shear waves that need rigid material. S-waves are slower than P-waves, so statement 2 is wrong. The absence of S-waves beyond 105 degrees is the key evidence for a liquid outer core.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 3

questions.q:
Match List-I (Discontinuity) with List-II (Boundary):
List-I
A. Mohorovicic
B. Gutenberg
C. Lehmann
D. Conrad
List-II
1. Between upper and lower crust
2. Between outer core and inner core
3. Between crust and mantle
4. Between mantle and outer core
questions.e: Moho marks the crust-mantle boundary, Gutenberg the mantle-core boundary at about 2,900 km, Lehmann the outer-inner core boundary, and Conrad the boundary within the crust.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 3
questions.h: Moho = top of mantle, Gutenberg = Gate to core

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Earth is at perihelion in early January.
2. The Earth is at aphelion in early July.
3. Seasons are caused chiefly by the tilt of the Earth's axis and its constant orientation in space.
4. Seasons are caused chiefly by the changing distance between the Earth and the Sun.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Earth is nearest the Sun around 3 January and farthest around 4 July. Seasons arise because the tilted axis keeps pointing the same way, so each hemisphere alternately leans towards the Sun. If distance mattered, the Northern summer would fall in January, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 9

questions.q: Which one of the following is a sedimentary rock?
questions.e: Dolomite is a carbonate rock formed by deposition and cementation of sediments. Gneiss and schist are formed by heat and pressure on granite or shale, and quartzite is metamorphosed sandstone.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about intrusive igneous forms:
1. A laccolith is a dome-shaped body with a flat base.
2. A lopolith is saucer-shaped.
3. A dyke cuts across the bedding of rocks.
4. A sill is a horizontal sheet that lies parallel to the bedding.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Magma pushes up overlying strata into a dome in a laccolith and sags into a basin in a lopolith. A dyke solidifies in a vertical crack across layers, while a sill spreads between layers.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 5 and Ch 7

questions.q:
Arrange the following karst depressions in increasing order of size:
1. Uvala
2. Polje
3. Doline
questions.e: Dolines (sinkholes) are small funnel-shaped hollows; several merge to form an uvala, and the largest, flat-floored depressions are poljes.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 7

questions.q: Which one of the following is a warm ocean current?
questions.e: The East Australian Current carries warm tropical water southward along the east coast. Falkland, West Australian and Benguela currents are cold currents flowing towards the equator along western or southern margins.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 14

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tides:
1. Spring tides occur at new moon and full moon.
2. Neap tides occur when the Sun, Earth and Moon form a right angle.
3. The highest tidal range in the world is recorded in the Bay of Biscay.
4. Successive high tides occur at intervals of exactly 12 hours.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: At new and full moon the Sun and Moon pull along one line, giving high spring tides; at quarter moon their pulls are at right angles and cancel partly, giving neap tides. The highest range is in the Bay of Fundy, and the interval between high tides is about 12 hours 26 minutes.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 14

questions.q: Which one of the following is the deepest trench in the Indian Ocean?
questions.e: The Java (Sunda) Trench, south of Indonesia, is the deepest part of the Indian Ocean. The other three trenches lie in the Pacific Ocean.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 13

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the troposphere and tropopause:
1. The tropopause is higher over the equator than over the poles.
2. The temperature at the equatorial tropopause is lower than that at the polar tropopause.
3. The ozone layer lies in the mesosphere.
questions.e: Strong convection lifts the troposphere to about 18 km at the equator, so air reaches a colder level (about -80 degrees C) than at the poles (about -45 degrees C), where the tropopause is lower. The ozone layer is in the stratosphere.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 8

questions.q:
Statement-I: Temperature inversion is most common on clear, calm winter nights.
Statement-II: On such nights the ground loses heat rapidly by terrestrial radiation and cools the air layer in contact with it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: With clear sky and no wind, nothing blocks outgoing radiation or mixes the air, so the surface and the air just above become colder than the layer higher up. This is why Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 9

questions.q: Out of 100 units of incoming solar radiation, how many units are absorbed by the Earth's surface in the heat budget described by NCERT?
questions.e: About 35 units are reflected back (albedo), 14 are absorbed by the atmosphere and 51 reach and are absorbed by the surface. The 65 units is the total absorbed (51 + 14).
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 9

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about jet streams:
1. The Tropical Easterly Jet is observed over peninsular India during the summer monsoon.
2. Jet streams are narrow bands of strong winds in the upper troposphere.
3. Jet streams are found in the stratosphere at a height of about 50 km.
questions.e: Jet streams lie near the tropopause at about 9-13 km, not in the stratosphere at 50 km. The easterly jet over the peninsula in summer is linked to strong heating of the Tibetan plateau.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 10; NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Tropical cyclone name : Region
1. Willy-willies : North-western Australia
2. Baguio : Mexico
3. Typhoon : Caribbean Sea
4. Hurricane : South China Sea
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Willy-willies is the Australian name. Baguio is used in the Philippines, typhoons occur in the western Pacific and China seas, and hurricanes occur in the Caribbean and Atlantic.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 10

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the pressure belts and winds is NOT correct?
o: Doldrums are a belt of calm and variable winds with rising air near the equator
Horse latitudes are subtropical high-pressure zones with descending air
Polar easterlies blow from the sub-polar low to the polar high
Westerlies blow from the subtropical high to the sub-polar low
questions.e: Winds always blow from high to low pressure. Polar easterlies therefore blow from the polar high towards the sub-polar low, so the stated direction is reversed.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 10

questions.q:
Match List-I (Local Wind) with List-II (Description):
List-I
A. Chinook
B. Mistral
C. Harmattan
D. Sirocco
List-II
1. Hot wind from the Sahara towards the Mediterranean
2. Dry dusty wind blowing from the Sahara over West Africa
3. Cold wind of southern France
4. Warm dry wind on the eastern slopes of the Rockies
questions.e: The Chinook is a warm down-slope wind east of the Rockies, the Mistral a cold wind funnelled down the Rhone valley, the Harmattan a dusty dry wind to the Gulf of Guinea coast, and the Sirocco a hot wind from the Sahara.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 10; Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Savanna climate:
1. It has distinct wet and dry seasons.
2. The Llanos of the Orinoco basin and the Campos of Brazil are savanna grasslands.
3. Its vegetation is mostly tall evergreen forest with a dense canopy.
questions.e: Alternating rainy and dry seasons favour tall grass with scattered drought-resistant trees, not dense evergreen forest, which belongs to the equatorial belt.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 12; Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q: Which one of the following regions of the world experiences the greatest annual range of temperature?
questions.e: Large landmass far from the oceans and long, clear winter nights cause extreme cold in winter and warm summers, so the annual range is highest in Siberia. Equatorial basins have very small ranges, and the Mediterranean coast is moderated by the sea.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 12; Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q:
Match List-I (Geological System of India) with List-II (Characteristic):
List-I
A. Archaean
B. Dharwar
C. Gondwana
D. Deccan Trap
List-II
1. Basaltic lava flows
2. Coal-bearing sedimentary rocks
3. Gneisses and schists
4. Metamorphic rocks with gold, iron ore and manganese
questions.e: The Archaean system is the primitive crystalline gneiss and schist base. The Dharwar system, the oldest metamorphosed sediments, carries gold, iron ore and manganese; the Gondwana beds hold most of India's coal; and the Deccan Trap is a basalt outpouring.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 2; Majid Husain

questions.q: The Karewa formations of the Kashmir Valley are
o: thick lake deposits laid down when the valley was a lake, and later useful for saffron cultivation
moraine ridges left by glaciers in Ladakh
wind-blown loess deposits of the Potwar plateau
alluvial fans of the Terai belt
questions.e: The Pir Panjal uplift once blocked the drainage of the valley and turned it into a lake, where silt and clay accumulated; these lake beds form the Karewas, which are used for saffron, almonds and other crops.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 2; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Mountain pass : State
1. Shipki La : Himachal Pradesh
2. Bomdi La : Arunachal Pradesh
3. Nathu La : Sikkim
4. Lipulekh : Sikkim
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Shipki La (Sutlej valley), Bomdi La (near Tawang) and Nathu La (to Tibet) are correctly placed. Lipulekh is in Uttarakhand, on the route to Kailash Mansarovar.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Peninsular plateau:
1. Anamudi is the highest peak of Peninsular India.
2. The Eastern Ghats are continuous and unbroken.
3. The Palghat Gap lies between the Nilgiri hills and the Anaimalai hills.
questions.e: Anamudi (about 2,695 m) in the Anaimalai hills of Kerala is the highest peak south of the Himalaya. The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous because the Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna and Cauvery have cut through them.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Match List-I (Channel) with List-II (Separates):
List-I
A. Ten Degree Channel
B. Nine Degree Channel
C. Eight Degree Channel
List-II
1. Minicoy and the Maldives
2. Minicoy and the main Lakshadweep group
3. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
questions.e: The channels are named after the latitude they follow: 10 degrees N divides the Andaman group from the Nicobar group, 9 degrees N separates Minicoy from the rest of Lakshadweep, and 8 degrees N separates Minicoy from the Maldives.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about lagoons in India:
1. Chilika Lake is located in Andhra Pradesh.
2. Pulicat Lake lies on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
3. Vembanad is a lagoon in Kerala.
questions.e: Chilika, the largest coastal lagoon, is in Odisha. Pulicat is a lagoon on the Andhra-Tamil Nadu coast and Vembanad is the largest of the Kerala backwaters.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Arrange the following confluences (prayags) in the order met while going downstream along the Alaknanda:
Vishnuprayag, Nandaprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, Devprayag
questions.e: The Dhauliganga, Nandakini, Pindar and Mandakini join the Alaknanda in that order, and the Alaknanda finally meets the Bhagirathi at Devprayag to form the Ganga.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 3; Majid Husain
questions.h: Vishnu, Nanda, Karna, Rudra, Deva: V-N-K-R-D

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Narmada and Tapi:
1. Both flow westward through rift valleys.
2. The Narmada drains into the Bay of Bengal.
3. The Tapi rises near Multai in the Betul district.
questions.e: Both rivers run in faulted troughs and fall into the Arabian Sea, forming estuaries instead of deltas. The Narmada does not reach the Bay of Bengal.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about local weather phenomena of India:
1. Mango showers help the ripening of mangoes in Kerala and Karnataka.
2. Kalbaisakhi nor'westers occur in West Bengal in the pre-monsoon season.
3. The Loo is a cold, dry wind of the winter season.
4. Blossom showers help the growth of tea in Assam.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Mango showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka and the Kalbaisakhi storms of Bengal are pre-monsoon events. The Loo is a hot dry summer wind of the northern plains, and blossom showers favour coffee in Kerala and Karnataka.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Statement-I: Western disturbances bring winter rainfall to north-western India.
Statement-II: They are extratropical cyclonic systems that originate over the Mediterranean region and are steered eastwards by the westerly jet stream.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Moist air carried from the Mediterranean towards Iran, Pakistan and India is lifted by the Himalaya, which gives winter rain and snow. This steering mechanism explains why the rain reaches north-western India.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about teleconnections and the Indian monsoon:
1. El Nino is characterised by the cooling of the eastern Pacific Ocean.
2. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is generally favourable to Indian monsoon rainfall.
3. La Nina conditions are generally favourable to the Indian monsoon.
questions.e: El Nino is a warming of the eastern Pacific, which weakens the Walker circulation and usually the monsoon. A positive IOD, with a warmer western Indian Ocean, and La Nina generally favour good rain.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Match List-I (Koppen Type) with List-II (Region of India):
List-I
A. Amw
B. As
C. BWhw
D. Dfc
List-II
1. Most of western Rajasthan
2. Arunachal Pradesh
3. West coast south of Mumbai
4. Coromandel coast
questions.e: Amw (monsoon with a short dry season) fits the wet Malabar coast, As (dry summer) the Coromandel coast that gets its rain in winter, BWhw the hot desert of the west, and Dfc the cold, humid-winter climate of the eastern Himalaya.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian forest types:
1. Tropical wet evergreen forests occur in areas receiving more than 200 cm of rainfall.
2. Tropical moist deciduous forests, with teak and sal, receive about 100-200 cm of rainfall.
3. Teak is the dominant tree of tropical thorn forests.
questions.e: Rainfall decides the forest type: very heavy rain gives evergreen forest and moderate rain deciduous forest with teak and sal. Thorn forests grow in dry areas with less than about 70 cm and are dominated by acacias and similar thorny trees.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 5

questions.q:
Match List-I (Mediterranean Scrub) with List-II (Region):
List-I
A. Chaparral
B. Matorral
C. Fynbos
D. Mallee
List-II
1. South Africa
2. Chile
3. Australia
4. California
questions.e: Dry summers produce hard-leaved, drought-resistant scrub in each Mediterranean region: chaparral in California, matorral in central Chile, fynbos in the south-western Cape and mallee in southern Australia.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 12; Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of National Park and animal is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Periyar in Kerala is known for elephants and tigers; the one-horned rhinoceros lives in the Brahmaputra floodplain at Kaziranga and Manas. Hangul, sangai and the Asiatic lion are correctly paired.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 5; Shankar IAS

questions.q:
Statement-I: Chernozems of the temperate grasslands are among the most fertile soils of the world.
Statement-II: Podzols develop under coniferous forests.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Chernozems are rich in humus because grass roots add organic matter every year. Podzols form under conifers, where acidic litter leaches the topsoil, but this has no bearing on chernozem fertility.
questions.s: Certificate Physical Geography; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian soils:
1. Kari soils of Kerala are peaty and rich in organic matter.
2. Red soils owe their colour to a high proportion of calcium.
3. Saline soils, called Reh, Kallar or Usar, contain large amounts of sodium, potassium and magnesium salts.
questions.e: Red soils are coloured by iron oxide diffused through crystalline rocks, not calcium. Waterlogged conditions in Kerala preserve plant matter as peat, while salt build-up in dry irrigated areas creates the Reh and Usar soils.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6

questions.q: Which Union Territory recorded the lowest sex ratio in Census 2011?
questions.e: Daman and Diu had 618 females per 1,000 males, the lowest of all States and UTs, due to male migration for work. Dadra and Nagar Haveli (774), Chandigarh (818) and Delhi (868) were higher.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Arrange the following urban agglomerations in descending order of population in Census 2011:
1. Chennai
2. Delhi
3. Kolkata
4. Greater Mumbai
questions.e: Greater Mumbai (about 18.4 million) led, followed by Delhi (about 16.3 million), Kolkata (about 14.1 million) and Chennai (about 8.7 million).
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 4

questions.q: Which State recorded the highest decadal growth rate of population among the States in Census 2011?
questions.e: Meghalaya grew by about 27.95 percent between 2001 and 2011, ahead of Arunachal Pradesh (about 26 percent) and Bihar. Among the Union Territories, Dadra and Nagar Haveli grew faster.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Match List-I (Mining Centre) with List-II (Mineral):
List-I
A. Khetri
B. Jaduguda
C. Bailadila
D. Panna
List-II
1. Uranium
2. Iron ore
3. Diamond
4. Copper
questions.e: Khetri in Rajasthan is a copper centre, Jaduguda in Jharkhand a uranium mine, Bailadila in Chhattisgarh a high-grade iron ore field, and Panna in Madhya Pradesh the diamond belt.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 7

questions.q: Which one of the following nuclear power stations is NOT correctly matched with its State?
questions.e: Rawatbhata (Rajasthan Atomic Power Station) is in Rajasthan, on the Chambal river. Narora, Kaiga and Kakrapar are in the States named.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 7

questions.q: Which one of the following iron and steel plants is NOT correctly matched with the foreign collaborator that helped to set it up?
questions.e: Bokaro, like Bhilai, was built with Soviet help. Rourkela was set up with German firms and Durgapur with British assistance during the Second Five Year Plan.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 8
questions.h: Bhilai and Bokaro: both B, both Soviet

questions.q:
Statement-I: Alumina refineries are usually located close to bauxite mines.
Statement-II: Bauxite loses a large part of its weight when it is refined into alumina.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because bauxite is a weight-losing raw material, refining it near the mine saves transport cost on the waste. The weight loss in refining is therefore exactly why the refineries stay near the mines.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 8; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about railway gauges in India:
1. The broad gauge is 1.676 m wide.
2. The metre gauge is 1.067 m wide.
3. 762 mm is one of the narrow gauge widths.
questions.e: Broad gauge is 1,676 mm and metre gauge is 1,000 mm. Narrow gauge is 762 mm (2 ft 6 in) or 610 mm.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 10

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Border Roads Organisation functions under the Ministry of Defence.
2. The Sagarmala programme aims at port-led development.
3. Bharatmala is a programme mainly for developing inland waterways.
questions.e: BRO builds roads in border areas and works under the Defence Ministry, and Sagarmala promotes port modernisation and coastal development. Bharatmala is a highways programme, not for inland waterways.
questions.s: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways; Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

questions.q:
Which of the following are Rabi crops?
1. Gram
2. Mustard
3. Cotton
4. Barley
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Rabi crops are sown in October-December and harvested in spring; gram, mustard and barley fit this pattern. Cotton is a kharif crop, sown with the monsoon.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about plantation crops in India:
1. Tamil Nadu is the largest producer of coffee.
2. Assam is the largest producer of tea.
3. Kerala is the largest producer of natural rubber.
questions.e: Karnataka grows most of India's coffee, mainly in Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan. Assam leads in tea and Kerala in natural rubber.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q: The approximate length of one degree of longitude at 60 degrees North latitude is
questions.e: Meridians converge towards the poles, so one degree of longitude shrinks in proportion to the cosine of latitude. Cosine 60 degrees is 0.5, giving about half of the 111 km at the equator.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography

questions.q: On a map of scale 1:25,000, a road measures 12 cm. Its actual length is
questions.e: At 1:25,000, 1 cm on the map equals 25,000 cm = 250 m on the ground. Twelve centimetres thus equal 3,000 m = 3 km.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography
